newsitem.title: USA: Dry week to follow weekend rain in U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Dry week to follow weekend rain in U.S. Midwest.

text.p: Late Sunday rain of 0.5 to 2.0 inches across Missouri, eastern Iowa, and the northern halves of Illinois, Indiana and Ohio should be replaced by dry cool weather from Tuesday to Friday, meteorologists said.
"The western belt is already turning cooler," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.
By Tuesday, much of the Midwest should be cool with high temperatures ranging from the upper 50s degrees Fahrenheit across the northern tier to 70s across the south, he said.
Lows could dip into the mid-30s from Minnesota to Michigan, and 40s elsewhere.
However, meteorologists said they doubt the cold presents a threat to Midwest crops.
Rain could return late this week, moving west to east with amounts of 0.3 to 1.5 inches likely, Burgio said.

Fred Gesser, Weather Express Inc meteorologist, said weather maps suggest moderate to heavy rain amounts could occur Friday into early next week across the Plains, Midwest and mid-South regions. The rain should move west to east and then into the southeast U.S.

Gesser said the weather will remain cool with below-normal temperatures extending well into next week as a low pressure system over the Hudson Bay was preventing warm weather from entering the Midwest.
